html:
The Mongolian Revolution of 1921 drove Chinese troops and then the White Russian warlord Ungern-Sternberg from Mongolia, and set up a government of the Mongolian People's Party, backed by Soviet Russia, in Urga on 11 July 1921.

Its leader in the field was Damdin Sukhbaatar. At first the Bogd Khan stayed on as a limited monarch. When he died in 1924, the Mongolian People's Republic was declared, the second communist state in the world, and Urga was renamed Ulaanbaatar, Red Hero.

Mongolia stayed formally independent of China but became a close Soviet satellite. Under Choibalsan in the 1930s the monasteries were destroyed. Soviet rule ended with the democratic revolution of 1990.
